subject: science
intro: Stars are where most of the elements are made. Through nuclear fusion, stars fuse hydrogen into helium and then fuse heavier elements like carbon and oxygen in their cores. The heaviest elements, like gold and uranium, are produced in the powerful explosions of large stars called supernovas. These elements are then spread through space and can become part of new stars, planets, and even living things. So the atoms in our bodies were made in stars.

items.prompt: How are elements heavier than hydrogen first made in stars?

steps: Through fusion, stars join nuclei to form heavier elements like helium, carbon, and oxygen.
So heavier elements are made by nuclear fusion in stars.
solution.answer: Through nuclear fusion, which joins lighter nuclei into heavier elements like helium, carbon, and oxygen.

items.prompt: Where are the heaviest elements, like gold and uranium, produced?

steps: Ordinary fusion in a star's core makes elements up to around iron.
The heaviest elements need the extreme energy of a star exploding.
They are produced in supernovas, the explosions of large stars.
solution.answer: In supernovas, the powerful explosions of large stars.

items.prompt: How can the atoms in your body have come from stars?

steps: Stars make the elements through fusion and supernova explosions.
These elements spread through space and become part of new planets and living things.
So the atoms in your body were made in stars long ago.
solution.answer: Stars made the elements and spread them through space, where they became part of planets and living things, including your body.

items.prompt: What process in stars forms elements?

steps: Stars join nuclei together to form heavier elements.

items.prompt: Why can new stars and planets contain heavy elements?

steps: Earlier stars made heavy elements and spread them when they exploded.
This enriched the material in space with heavy elements.
New stars and planets form from that material, so they contain heavy elements.
solution.answer: Because earlier stars made and spread heavy elements, and new stars and planets form from that enriched material.

items.prompt: Communicate how the variety of elements in the universe was produced.

steps: Stars fuse hydrogen into helium and then into heavier elements up to around iron.
Supernova explosions produce the heaviest elements.
These elements spread through space, so stars and their explosions produced the variety of elements we see.
solution.answer: Stars produce elements by fusion up to around iron, and supernovas make the heaviest ones; these spread through space to form the variety of elements.
